title: Marius Remakes the Army
objective: After this level you can explain how Marius’s reforms tied soldiers to their generals.
summary: Seven-time consul Marius opened the legions to landless volunteers paid by the state. Soldiers began to look to generals, not the Senate.

cards.headline: The man who saved Rome from invaders also changed whom its soldiers served.
An army of the poor
cards.body: Gaius Marius was elected consul an unprecedented seven times. Facing a shortage of recruits, he enrolled poor citizens with no property, equipped and paid by the state. He led them to victory over the invading Cimbri and Teutones in 102 and 101 BCE.

cards.headline: Loyal to the general
cards.body: The new soldiers had no farms to return to. They looked to their general, not the Senate, for pay and for land when they retired. An army that depended on its commander could be turned against Rome itself.

cards.context: Marius made the silver eagle, the aquila, the standard of every legion. Losing it in battle was a disgrace.

questions.prompt: How many times was Marius elected consul?

options.label: Once
options.rationale: He held it far more often.

options.label: Twice
options.rationale: He held it far more often.

questions.explanation: Marius was elected consul an unprecedented seven times.

questions.prompt: Why did Marius’s reforms become a threat to the Republic?

options.label: Soldiers refused to fight in distant provinces
Soldiers served their general rather than the Senate
The army became too small to defend Italy
Generals could no longer command legions

questions.explanation: Landless soldiers depended on their commander for pay and land, so their loyalty followed him.

questions.prompt: From Level 29: whom had legions recruited before Marius?

options.label: Only enslaved people bought at auction
Foreign mercenaries hired from Greece and Gaul
Property-owning citizens with their own gear
Anyone at all who volunteered to serve

questions.explanation: Earlier legionaries were property-owning citizens who bought their own equipment; Marius opened the ranks to the landless.
